defects: Produced statement only assumes [Preorder α] [TopologicalSpace α], dropping the gold's [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [OrderTopology α] [DenselyOrdered α] — a Preorder is far weaker than a linear order and lacks the order-completeness needed for the fixed-point argument; the statement is not even total-order, so 'Icc a b' need not behave as an interval and the theorem is false/unprovable in this generality
No LinearOrder assumption at all, so a ≤ b and Icc a b lack the totality the informal statement (and gold) implicitly rely on
Missing OrderTopology linking the order and topology, so ContinuousOn has no guaranteed relationship to order structure
Missing DenselyOrdered, which is needed for the density argument underlying the classical proof of this fixed-point result
